newsitem.title: UK: MERSEY DOCKS TO KEEP INVESTING FOR FUTURE.
newsitem.headline: MERSEY DOCKS TO KEEP INVESTING FOR FUTURE.

text.p: British port operator Mersey Docks and Harbour Co, which saw a 59.4 percent jump in half year profits, said on Thursday it will continue investing to boost growth prospects.
"The group has and will continue to invest to augment profitability in the future and has the financial strength to do so," the company said in its results statement.
It said a number of developments have been initiated to "enhance its platform for growth".

These include work which has started at Liverpool on the first phase of development of a 860,000 sq ft of warehousing and light industrial units, and work to commence shortly on a new deep water berth and storage complex at Medway.

It said phase one of the Sheerness Produce Terminal's complex was destroyed by fire on August 4. The building was fully insured and the group is now seeking storage space at Port of Sheerness in Kent.
The second phase of the 15 million stg work continues and is scheduled to be completed in the second half of 1997.

Referring to the long-running labour dispute with sacked dock workers at Liverpool, the operator said while its impact on profitability was "not material" the fact it is still not resolved "remains of concern not only to your group but to Merseyside as a whole".

Mersey Docks reported pre-tax profits of 22.2 million stg in the six months to June 30, up from 13.9 million in the same period the year before. It proposed an interim dividend of 4.5 pence, up 12.5 percent.

It said the results reflect the strength of its business at Liverpool and Medway as well as the good performance of its Irish Sea service. It also benefited from the absence of losses at its Eurolink Ferry service which it terminated in December last year.
